main_issue: Whether and how Agent D may keep cooking strong-smelling sambal in the shared kitchen (ban vs. warning vs. limiting frequency/day), given smell in rooms, living room and laundry

A-B.evidence: A wants a ban, later Saturday-only (T1, T22); B only wants a warning and says the day doesn't matter (T25); A says a warning doesn't help the living room (T20). Both want D to curb the smell but they favour different fixes.

A-C.evidence: Both are bothered by the smell (T3, T5); C says a warning doesn't help the laundry (T9), A says it doesn't help the living room (T20). C never takes a position on the Saturday proposal, and A says others can speak for themselves (T24).

A-D.evidence: D resists the ban (T4, T10, T12), then offers to cook once a week (T21). A calls that better and proposes Saturday (T22). D asks about B and C instead of accepting (T23), so there is no final agreement.

B-C.evidence: B calls the laundry a 'different problem' (T16) and C says it's the same smell (T17). B keeps pushing the warning, which C says doesn't help the laundry (T9).

B-D.evidence: B asks D repeatedly for a warning (T8, T14, T18). D deflects with C's laundry and asks whether the warning would be a house rule (T15, T19), but never refuses it outright. D asks what works for B (T23), and B answers that a warning is all he needs (T25).

C-D.evidence: D raises C's laundry (T15), which looks sympathetic, and asks what works for C (T23). C never answers and never responds to the once-a-week offer, so there is no clear agreement.
